sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Rana Tharu language' (raw wikitext, accessed 2026-09-17), summarising Ethnologue (thr) and Dhakal 2013/2015
sources.note: Secondary only: says the language 'lacks tonality' and has 28 consonant and 11 vowel phonemes; nothing on stress. Ethnologue page itself could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Dhakal, Dubi Nanda. 2015. Verb agreement in Rana Tharu. Nepalese Linguistics 30: 50-59.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology; morphosyntax only. Its bibliography lists Dhakal 2013 (Nepal Academy documentation report), Dhakal 2014b (LINCOM texts+sketch), Dhakal 2015 (Rana Tharu Grammar, Nepal Academy), Boehm 1998, Regmi/Thakur/Regmi 2012 (LinSuN survey), Rana, Amita 2066 VS primers.

sources.citation: Dhakal, Dubi Nanda. n.d. [data 2013-2014; text cited as Dhakal 2014b/2015]. Notes on Rana Tharu grammar. Manuscript grammar sketch (Chapter 1 Introduction, Chapter 2 'A Grammatical sketch of Rana Tharu', ms. pp. 5-49); by content the preprint of Dhakal 2015, Analyzed Texts in Rana Tharu (with a Grammatical Sketch), München: LINCOM (LW/T 36). Academia.edu item 43908543.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on word stress: 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the ~97k-character sketch. §2.1 Phonology covers vowels, consonants, clusters and syllable structure; the only suprasegmental statement (§2.1.4, ms. p. 12) is 'Rana Tharu is a non-tonal language. Generally, the questions have rising intonation and the statements have falling intonation.' Later (§2.3) 'Yes-no questions are indicated by rising intonation.'

sources.note: Only the two Dhakal articles above are on Rana Tharu; no Rana Tharu phonology paper in the run. Volume 23 has Boehm 2008 on Dangaura Tharu case marking (different language).
